CDISC Pilot 5 Automation Showcase

Source: vignettes/articles/cdisc-pilot-showcase.Rmd
cdisc-pilot-showcase.Rmd

Question: given the real CDISC pilot 5 data and the real submission ADaM spec, how far does admiralagent (+ DeepSeek as the translation backend) get on its own — and where exactly is the boundary?

This article is the narrative version of demo/automation/REPORT.md in the package repository, generated by a one-command, re-runnable pipeline:

Rscript demo/automation/run_all.R                  # cached LLM results reused
AA_FORCE_LLM=1 Rscript demo/automation/run_all.R   # re-spend on DeepSeek

Every number below is read from a machine-readable file under demo/automation/out/ (cited per section in the report). Nothing is typed in by hand, and the LLM never writes R code anywhere in the pipeline: DeepSeek only translates spec free text into the closed-vocabulary Layer IR (build_context() sends schema-level spec text only — never patient data); a deterministic compiler renders the admiral code.

The pipeline

Six staged, idempotent scripts under demo/automation/:

stage script what it does
00 00_ingest.R Builds the ADSL spec from the pilot5 submission’s P21-style define workbook (adam-pilot-5.xlsx, 49 ADSL variables: 47 derivations verbatim from the Methods sheet, 2 mechanical Copied directly from <DS.VAR> predecessor copies). Loads the original SDTM .xpt files; records sha256 digests of every input.
01 01_classify.R Classifies the same spec twice: backend = "rules" (zero-cost keyword baseline) and backend = "llm" (DeepSeek deepseek-chat). A deterministic 12-variable subset additionally runs samples = 3, consensus = "majority". Latency and token usage are recorded.
02 02_gate_render.R validate_ir() gate, then program + per-variable artifacts. Written with require_gate = FALSE — an explicit, recorded opt-out (no human approver in an unattended run); every program carries the UNGATED DRAFT banner and release_grade = "ungated-draft".
03 03_execute.R execute_ir() against the real pilot5 SDTM, run_validation(), hash-chained audit logs.
04 04_oracle_compare.R Variable-by-variable comparison against the submitted oracle original-adamdata/adsl.xpt.
05 05_report.R Assembles REPORT.md from the out/ files only.

What automated cleanly

From the run behind this article (out/gate_report.json, out/exec_status_<backend>.csv, out/accuracy_summary.json):

backend spec vars needs_human executed exec errors oracle: compared oracle: full match
rules 49 32 16 1 15 15 (100%)
LLM (DeepSeek) 49 27 20 2 19 16 (mean agreement 90.9%)

The picture that emerges is a coverage/automation trade-off, not a winner:

  • The rules baseline abstains on two-thirds of a real spec (32/49) — but every variable it did derive matched the oracle exactly.
  • DeepSeek automates meaningfully more (20 executed vs 16), and the extra variables it took on are exactly where the residual disagreement lives — see below.
  • Rules-vs-LLM layer chains agreed on 40/49 variables (82%) — IR-level agreement between two translators reading the same text, not double programming (see Limitations).
  • The 3-sample consensus run on the 12-variable subset was unanimous on 12/12 variables.
  • Cost is a rounding error: the full 49-variable run used 5,505 input / 7,083 output tokens in 84s — ≈ $0.009 at list prices (rate assumption recorded in out/llm_telemetry.json).

What needed humans — and why that is the point

The LLM abstained on 27/49 variables with a stated rationale each (REPORT.md §8). Grouped, the inventory is not random — it is the vocabulary boundary, stated out loud:

  • No conditional layer: SAFFL, ITTFL, DISCONFL, DSRAEFL, EOSSTT, and the COMP8/16/24FL visit-window flags are all Y if <condition> derivations. The vocabulary has no conditional/ifelse layer, so the model abstains instead of inventing one.
  • External references: SITEGR1 (defers to SAP §7.1), DCSREAS (an unstated grouping scheme), TRT01PN/TRT01AN (treatment codelist not in the spec).
  • Cross-dataset existence: EFFFL (QS records for two instruments), VISNUMEN (DS-conditioned), MMSETOT (subject-level sum over QS).
  • Multi-branch clinical logic: CUMDOSE’s arm-conditional dosing-interval arithmetic.

A system that hallucinated these would be worse than one that abstains. Fail-closed is the feature.

What failed, and the findings it produced

Per the improvement-loop convention, every error class became a numbered finding with evidence (out/findings.json, REPORT.md §9):

  • F-01 (package) — an LLM chain merge_var(SVSTDTC → TRTSDT) followed by impute_dtc(dtc = SVSTDTC) passes validate_ir() but fails at execution, because the merge renamed the column away. The fail-closed execution layer caught it; the semantic gate could catch it earlier. Registered as a package defect.
  • F-02 (demo config) — codelist_var needs a metacore object (sources$mc) the showcase didn’t build; RACEN-class derivations error at execution. Pipeline configuration gap, not an IR error.
  • F-03 (package) — the rules backend mapped BMIBLGR1’s categorisation text to compute_param on BMI keywords. Keyword fragility, documented as such.
  • F-04 (spec ambiguity) — AGEGR1N: in an earlier run all 11/254 mismatches were subjects aged exactly 80; the spec says both “65–80” and “>80”. A human programmer would have to query the same boundary.
  • F-05 (oracle convention) — HEIGHTBL/WEIGHTBL raw agreement is 19.7%/8.7%, but 98.8%/94.5% at the oracle’s own storage precision: the oracle rounds to 1 decimal and the spec never says so. BMIBL’s 99.6% inherits the same rounding. The derivations are semantically correct.

Also observed across development runs: DeepSeek’s full-spec needs_human count moved 24 → 22 → 27 and rules/LLM agreement 78% → 71% → 82% between runs. Translation variance is real, visible, and exactly what the consensus mode exists to measure.

Limitations (verbatim from the report — read before quoting any number)

  1. Population subsetting is not automated. Produced ADSL starts from DM (all screened subjects); the oracle has 254 randomized subjects. Agreement is computed on the join only.
  2. Vocabulary gaps are hard boundaries. No conditional/windowing layers; COMP*FL, EFFFL, CUMDOSE, ADTTE-style CNSR can only abstain or be approximated. More voters cannot fix a vocabulary hole.
  3. The rules backend is keyword-fragile. It is a zero-cost baseline, not a claim of understanding.
  4. The evals corpus is self-scoring. inst/evals/spec-to-ir.jsonl expected values were generated by the rules backend; it pins current behavior as contract, it is not an oracle.
  5. IR agreement ≠ double programming. All voters read the same spec text.
  6. Oracle differences may be spec ambiguity, not package error. Disagreement rates here are not error rates.
  7. Programs are UNGATED DRAFTs. No human approval gate covers them; they are demonstration output, not release-grade deliverables.
  8. Single model, single dataset, and stochastic. Numbers are DeepSeek deepseek-chat on pilot5 ADSL only, and LLM output varies run to run.

Reproduce 

git clone https://github.com/yanmingyu92/admiralagent
cd admiralagent
Rscript demo/automation/run_all.R

The pipeline reads the public CDISC pilot 5 data from a sibling cdisc_data/ directory (see demo/automation/_common.R for paths), and needs a DEEPSEEK_API_KEY only for the LLM stage — the rules-baseline stages run fully offline. Full evidence trail: demo/automation/REPORT.md + demo/automation/out/ in the repository.
